extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and legal counsel handling reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements the USPTO applies when imposing reciprocal discipline based on a state's disciplinary adjudication ( Selling v. Radford framework), including when identical discipline is imposed, the narrow scope of review, nunc pro tunc eligibility, and publication/notification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal-discipline presumption (Selling v. Radford)
rubrics_metrics.description: State discipline creates a federal-level presumption that imposition of reciprocal discipline is proper (citing Selling v. Radford, 243 U.S. 46 (1917)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Selling the USPTO presumes reciprocal discipline appropriate unless an independent review of the record reveals: (1) a want of due process; (2) an infirmity of proof of the misconduct; or (3) that grave injustice would result. The USPTO regulation mirrors this presumption (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to avoid reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)(i)-(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall impose identical discipline unless the practitioner clearly and convincingly demonstrates, and the Director finds there is a genuine issue of material fact that: (i) the procedure elsewhere was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute a deprivation of due process; (ii) there was such infirmity of proof establishing the conduct as to give rise to the clear conviction that the Office could not, consistently with its duty, accept as final the conclusion on that subject; (iii) the imposition of the same ... by the Office would result in a grave injustice; or (iv) any argument that the practitioner was not publicly censured, publicly reprimanded, placed on probation, disbarred, suspended or disciplinarily disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed ground is exclusive and must be shown to raise a genuine issue of material fact by clear and convincing evidence to prevent identical reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and standard of proof to overcome the presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the respondent-attorney's burden to demonstrate, by clear and convincing evidence, that one of the Selling/§11.24 exceptions precludes reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal courts and the USPTO apply a narrow standard; respondent must present clear and convincing evidence of a genuine issue of material fact. Case citations (e.g., In re Kramer, In re Friedman) reinforce that the showing is stringent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limitation of USPTO review
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO (and Director) does not act as a court of review to discover error in the state-court proceedings; review is limited to determining whether Selling/§11.24 exceptions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoting precedent: the USPTO is 'not sitting as a court of review to discover error' in the state courts' proceedings. The review is therefore narrow and focused on the three (or four) identified exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of identical discipline (types of discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall impose the identical public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, or disciplinary disqualification imposed by the other jurisdiction unless an exception is proven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identical-discipline requirement means the same form of public sanction is normally imposed by the USPTO; the Director's authority is to mirror the state-imposed sanction absent successful challenge under §11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely filed response consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall consider any timely filed response to the Notice and Complaint pursuant to §11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely response may include admissions, objections, factual submissions, and requests (e.g., requests to credit previously completed conditions); the Director will consider such materials when applying §11.24 standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nunc pro tunc (nune pro tune) reciprocal-discipline eligibility (§11.24(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed nunc pro tunc only if, upon request by the practitioner, the practitioner promptly notified the OED Director of the other-jurisdiction discipline and establishes by clear and convincing evidence that the practitioner voluntarily ceased all activities related to practice before the Office and complied with all provisions of §11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible for nunc pro tunc treatment a practitioner must: (1) promptly notify OED of the discipline; and (2) prove by clear and convincing evidence voluntary cessation of USPTO-related practice and compliance with §11.58. The effective date of a nunc pro tunc sanction is the date the practitioner ceased activities and complied with §11.58. Failure to meet these requirements precludes crediting state probation/suspension nunc pro tunc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit for prior completion of state-imposed conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of successful completion of state-imposed conditions (e.g., completion of probation, passing the MPRE) may be offered and considered when determining whether identical conditions should be included in USPTO discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the practitioner proves completion of a state-imposed condition, the Director may exclude that condition from the USPTO order (as with the MPRE here). However, crediting prior completion as running nunc pro tunc requires meeting §11.24(f)'s specific evidentiary and notice requirements; mere completion alone is insufficient for nunc pro tunc treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with §11.58 as a prerequisite for nunc pro tunc
rubrics_metrics.description: §11.24(f) requires that a practitioner who seeks nunc pro tunc discipline establish compliance with §11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although §11.58's detailed requirements are not restated on the page, the decision emphasizes that compliance with §11.58 is an explicit element the practitioner must prove by clear and convincing evidence to obtain nunc pro tunc effect; lack of such proof defeats the nunc pro tunc request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and reporting obligations following discipline (§11.59, Official Gazette, FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish notice of the discipline (e.g., in the Official Gazette) and give notice pursuant to §11.59 to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision requires publication of a Notice in the Official Gazette and makes the disciplinary decision available via the OED FOIA Reading Room (providing URL). These are mandatory post-discipline notification/publication steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdictional basis for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's authority to impose reciprocal discipline is grounded in 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and § 32, and implemented through 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision cites these statutory and regulatory bases to establish the USPTO's jurisdiction to entertain reciprocal-discipline complaints and issue orders mirroring other jurisdictions' sanctions.
